mission: The full scope lands: the Ruusan Reformations as penance, the forbidden technique, the wound at Veranthos, the anchor system, the Brotherhood's lattice inversion attempt. Delivered through Sera's precision, Torin's warmth, and Kael's dry corrections — not through narrator exposition.
why_now: The survivors recognise the archive and can read what Ben could not. The vocabulary returns with its original speakers, and the architecture finally has a name.
conflict: The information rewrites the foundational narrative of Ben's Order in front of him. Sera delivers the official account with professional precision; Torin warms the edges with lived memory; Kael corrects details from an angle neither of them expected.
turning_point: The Reformations — the foundation of modern Jedi identity — were penance and damage control. The Order Ben was raised inside has been built on what Gavran chose not to say.
opening_hook: Sera crosses to the archive console and her fingers find the activation sequence from muscle memory — a thousand years old and still faster than Ben's modern training
closing_hook: The technique. The wound. The seal. The anchors. Twelve Force-sensitives used as structural rebar in a containment system. Nine dead. Three just woken. One escaped.
emotional_trajectory: Absorbing shock -> intellectual vertigo -> moral reckoning with institutional history

stakes.personal: The account Ben grew up inside does not match the room he is standing in
stakes.interpersonal: The survivors' conflicting accounts reveal they were not all willing participants
stakes.external: The wound exists, the seal is failing, and the Order does not know any of this

setting: Fortress Level 2 (Archive) — survivors navigating familiar territory with thousand-year-old muscle memory
sensory_details: Archive media activating under Sera's touch; holographic displays showing the wound's expansion across centuries as a red accretion over the map; Torin's hand brushing a console with a familiarity that makes Ben's skin register wrong before his mind does; the Codex fragment resting faintly lit inside its sealed case
canon_elements_needed: Ruusan Reformations true historical purpose and aftermath
Brotherhood of Darkness organization and military doctrine
Force wound theory with Nihilus and Malachor V precedent
Institutional memory loss and generational knowledge gaps in the Jedi Order
Jedi Lords era Force techniques and capabilities
Light and dark side boundary theory in Legends metaphysics
action_beats: Sera activates the archive console with an ancient access code from muscle memory
Holographic displays bloom showing the wound's expansion over centuries — red zones growing across the map
Torin pulls the sealed Codex fragment from its housing and opens the case
Kael reaches past Sera to correct a detail on the projection map — his first voluntary contribution
promises_planted: The institutional lie must be told to the Order (PP08)
The Jacen parallel will be recognized (PP07)
notes: R04 is the First Plot Point revelation. Highest info-dump risk scene in the book — every piece of exposition must be earned through character reaction. Sera's precision, Torin's narrative warmth, Kael's dry corrections carry the history. When Sera explains something, Ben's internal response tells the reader why it matters; when Torin narrates, his warmth makes the history feel personal rather than academic; when Kael corrects, the uncomfortable authority of his angle should land for a beat before he lets it go. Prior-EU onboarding — Jacen surfaces here for the first time inside a historical briefing context. One grounding phrase, no recap. Ben's tone does the work; the reader who knows the reference feels the weight, the reader who does not learns it in context without the scene stopping for a footnote. Anti-pattern: no character delivers the thematic sentence about 'repeating the Lords' mistakes' — the point should emerge from what they each take from the same history, not from a speech.
